_about: Structured local version of the Commons Connect forms (ODK templates and Word drafts), with the atlas questions each one overlaps and a must-ask rule. Built by `python -m seft.cli cc-build --forms <folder>` (seft/commons_connect.py); scored by seft/priority.py and, in the browser, by the Commons Connect tab of web/index.html. Option ids are the values the ODK forms store.
built_from: commons_connect_forms.zip (12 ODK XLSForm templates, 15 Word documents)

sections.label: Landscape
sections.about: What the atlas infers about the micro-watershed, confirmed with the community.

sections.label: Resource mapping
sections.about: Transect walk: settlements, waterbodies, wells, crops and forest patches.

sections.label: Planning
sections.about: Demands for new works and for maintenance, ranked by what suits this landscape.

plan_groups.label: Surface waterbodies (maintenance; new ones are proposed as recharge or irrigation works)

priority.about: Each question gets a must-ask score from 0 to 100. Atlas questions are scored from the current inference (seft/priority.py); a Commons Connect question takes the highest of its own base score, the scores of the atlas questions it matches (times the weight for how closely they match), and the scores of its rules that hold here (a question with no base score, rule or match gets default_base). A routing question takes the highest score of the questions it leads to. Records (names, beneficiary details, dimensions, photos) are always kept and are not scored.
priority.stress_question: For every rule the question informs (and that applies here), with p its current probability: flip = the chance that the answer takes the rule across the positive line (positive_at): when some answer would do so, p if the rule is below the line (a supporting answer is needed) or 1 − p if above it, scaled so that 0.5 counts fully; move = the largest change in probability any answer would make (0.4 counts fully); uncertainty = 1 − |2p − 1|; borderline = how close the data are to the rule's threshold (for a triggered rule 1 − intensity/100, for a rule not triggered its partial intensity/100, 1 when the data are missing); low confidence = 1 for a low-confidence rule, 0.5 for medium. Rule score = 100 × (0.35 flip + 0.1 move + 0.15 uncertainty + 0.3 borderline + 0.1 low confidence). Question score = the highest rule score, plus 5 for each further rule scoring 50 or more. urg_<rule> is the score of a typical question for that rule, one with likelihood ratios 0.4 and 2.5.
priority.system_question: For each answer the system mix is recomputed. cross = for the systems some answer would take across their presence threshold (present_at), how close the share is to that threshold now (1 at the threshold, 0 at zero or twice the threshold), the largest; shift = the mean share of the MWS the answers would move (total variation; 0.15 counts fully). Score = 100 × (0.6 cross + 0.4 shift), or the stress score of its options if that is higher. A system question whose show_if fails scores 0.
priority.type_question: Waterbody type questions: for each answer the type is reassigned. Score = 100 × (0.6 if some answer changes the type + 0.4 × the share of answers that do).
priority.planning: A work type scores 90 when an intervention it builds suits this landscape and responds to a stress found here, 65 when it is possible and responds to a stress, 40 when it suits but no stress calls for it, 20 when it is only possible, and 5 when it is not suited. A work-type question and its form take the highest score of their work types.
priority.env: Rule conditions use the watershed variables, share_<system>, the context classes (rainfall, aquifer, terrain, gw_category, canal, cropping), ps_<production system> (1 present, 0 absent), p_<rule> (probability), pos_<rule> (1 when likely present), urg_<rule> (the rule's must-ask score) and ask_<atlas question>, with dots in rule ids written as double underscores (p_groundwater__over_extraction). In the waterbody form: the waterbody variables, wtype, wp_<rule>, wpos_<rule> and wask_<question>; in the MWS, n_wb and wbpos_<rule> (number of waterbodies where the rule is likely).
